overview: The arm animation packet is an empty swing signal and the only per-click client input anticheats see reliably, which makes it the primitive of every autoclicker check in the corpus. Statistical checks sample the number of movement packets between swings and flag low-variance or excessive click rates (Frequency AutoClickerA, FlopAC AutoClickerA, Hydro's ArmAnimationCheck family). It is also the swing half of swing-break correlation checks (Grim NoSwingBreak) that catch nuker clients breaking blocks without swinging.

checks.name: AutoClickerA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Classic low-deviation autoclicker check over the arm animation stream.
checks.how_it_works: Samples the number of flying packets between WrappedPlayInArmAnimation packets, keeping a deque of 20 movement gaps. Samples are only accepted when CPS is above 6.5, fewer than 4 movements separate clicks, and the player is neither digging nor placing. When 20 samples accumulate it computes the standard deviation and outlier count; a deviation below 2 with fewer than 2 outliers fails the check.
checks.detects: Autoclickers with mechanical timing, where the gap between swings has near-zero variance.
checks.variations: AutoClickerB through G in the same package add delay patterns, outlier ratios and CPS caps; Degrade's AutoClickerA and Hydro's AutoClickerA/B/C follow the same statistical template.

checks.name: NoSwingBreak (Grim)
checks.purpose: Swing-break correlation: every block break must be accompanied by an arm animation.
checks.how_it_works: Implements BlockBreakListener and PreViaPacketReceiveListener. It sets sentBreak on a non-cancelled break action, sets sentAnimation when the ANIMATION packet arrives, and on the next tick packet flags if a break was sent without an animation in between, then resets both flags.
checks.detects: Nuker and instamine clients that break blocks without sending swings, and killaura-style dig abuse.
checks.variations: NCP's NoSwing blockbreak check and BetterAnticheat's NoSwingDigCheck implement the same idea on Bukkit events and packet handlers respectively.

checks.name: ArmAnimationCheck base (Hydro)
checks.purpose: The shared base class of Hydro's whole autoclicker family: it converts the animation stream into click samples and CPS for per-check handlers.
checks.how_it_works: On each ANIMATION packet, if the action tracker is not digging, it records the movement gap into a click sample queue, applying filters for combat-only checks (last attack within a minute), double-click variants, and the zero-movement case. At the configured sample size it computes CPS via MathUtil and delegates to the abstract handle method, then clears the queue. Flying packets increment the movement counter.
checks.detects: Feeds the AutoClickerA/B/C and double-click checks that flag constant CPS and double-click patterns from the sampled gaps.
checks.variations: Intave's click-pattern checks (Deviation, Entropy, Kurtosis, Repetitive) and Artemis AutoClickerA-M run the same sampling with statistical distributions instead of fixed thresholds.

checks.name: AutoClickerA (FlopAC)
checks.purpose: CPS ceiling check: sustained clicking above 20 clicks per second is an autoclicker.
checks.how_it_works: Counts movements between ARM_ANIMATION packets into a delay list when fewer than 10 movements separate them. At 30 samples it converts the delays to CPS via MathUtil and flags when CPS exceeds 20, then clears the list. The sample resets while the player is digging, holding a block or sword, or for the first 60 ticks after join, keeping the check on combat clicks.
checks.detects: Autoclickers clicking above 20 CPS, including fast-click modules that fake the animation rate.
checks.variations: AutoClickerB through K in the same package add jitter, outlier and double-click checks; azure's AutoClickerA and LightAntiCheat's AutoClickerA use the same movement-gap template.
